questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a palpable mass in the left upper quadrant. Imaging shows a well‑defined, encapsulated lesion adjacent to the spleen. Which of the following structures is most likely to be involved if the mass originates from the organ of the left upper quadrant and is resected with a short segment of the adjacent organ?
questions.explanation: The lesion is most consistent with a pancreatic tail tumour, which lies adjacent to the spleen and is often resected with a splenectomy. The left adrenal gland and kidney are posterior and would not be involved in a typical upper‑quadrant mass. The splenic flexure of the colon is not in close contact with the pancreas and would not be resected with a pancreatic tail lesion.
questions.source: Anatomy of the upper abdomen; relationship of pancreas to adjacent organs
questions.topic: Anatomy of the upper abdomen; relationship of pancreas to adjacent organs
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures lies directly anterior to the pancreas?
questions.explanation: The common bile duct runs posterior to the first part of the duodenum and lies anterior to the pancreas. The splenic vein and portal vein are posterior, while the superior mesenteric artery is posterior and lateral. Thus option C is correct.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is the most superficial layer of the abdominal wall?
questions.explanation: The external oblique muscle lies on top of the internal oblique and transversus abdominis, making it the most superficial layer of the abdominal wall. The other muscles are deeper, and the rectus sheath encloses the rectus abdominis rather than forming a superficial layer.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: How are Infarcts anatomically classified based on their gross appearance and underlying vascular supply?
options: Primary infarcts versus secondary metastatic infarcts
questions.explanation: Infarcts are classified as white (solid organs with end-arterial supply like heart/spleen) or red (loose tissues/dual supply like lung/intestine).
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man undergoes a left hemicolectomy for a transverse colon carcinoma. In the operative field, the surgeon identifies a short, well‑defined arterial trunk that supplies the splenic flexure and drains into the superior mesenteric vein. Which of the following arteries is most likely being encountered?
questions.explanation: The splenic flexure is supplied by the left colic artery, a branch of the inferior mesenteric artery. It is a short, well‑defined trunk that often drains into the superior mesenteric vein via the marginal artery. The sigmoid artery supplies the sigmoid colon, the ileocolic artery supplies the terminal ileum and cecum, and the marginal artery is a continuous arcade rather than a single trunk.
questions.source: Colonic arterial supply; standard surgical anatomy
questions.topic: Colonic arterial supply; standard surgical anatomy
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: A patient suffers a deep glass laceration on the volar aspect of the wrist just medial to the flexor carpi radialis tendon. Which nerve is most likely severed, and what is the primary functional deficit?
options: Ulnar nerve; loss of finger abduction/adduction
Median nerve; paralysis of thenar muscles (loss of thumb opposition—ape hand) and anesthesia of the palmar lateral 3½ digits
Musculocutaneous nerve; loss of elbow flexion
questions.explanation: The median nerve lies immediately medial to the flexor carpi radialis tendon (and deep to palmaris longus) just proximal to the carpal tunnel; laceration here causes ape-hand deformity, loss of thumb opposition, and sensory loss over the lateral 3½ digits.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: A patient sustains a penetrating stab wound to the femoral triangle just lateral to the femoral artery. Which nerve is injured, and what motor deficit results?
options: Obturator nerve; loss of thigh adduction
Femoral nerve; paralysis of quadriceps femoris (loss of knee extension) and weakened hip flexion, with absent patellar reflex
Sciatic nerve; loss of knee flexion and foot drop
Common peroneal nerve; loss of foot eversion
questions.explanation: The femoral nerve lies immediately lateral to the femoral artery (outside the femoral sheath) in the femoral triangle; its injury paralyzes the quadriceps, abolishes knee extension and the patellar jerk, and causes sensory loss over the anterior thigh and medial leg.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Alcock’s canal (pudendal canal) is located within the lateral wall of the ischiorectal fossa and is formed by a splitting of:
questions.explanation: Alcock’s canal is a fascial tunnel within the obturator fascia on the lateral wall of the ischiorectal fossa.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: An abscess located in the ischiorectal fossa typically causes:
options: Throbbing perianal pain aggravated by sitting, with localized swelling/erythema
questions.explanation: Ischiorectal abscesses fill the fossa with pus, producing marked systemic sepsis signs, throbbing pain, and fluctuant swelling beside the anus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: An infection on the lateral border of the heel is most likely to cause tender lymphadenopathy initially in which group?
questions.explanation: Lymph from the lateral foot/heel tracks along the small saphenous vein directly to the popliteal lymph nodes.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Anal fissures most commonly occur at which anatomical clock position due to poor local perfusion?
questions.explanation: Over 85-90% of typical anal fissures occur in the posterior midline because of relatively sparse blood perfusion in that zone.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: At what anatomical level does the brachial artery terminate by dividing into the radial and ulnar arteries?
options: At the lower border of teres major
In the cubital fossa at the level of the neck of the radius
At the flexor retinaculum of the wrist
questions.explanation: The brachial artery bifurcates into the radial and ulnar arteries opposite the neck of the radius in the distal cubital fossa.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: At what landmark does the anterior tibial artery continue as the dorsalis pedis artery?
options: Midway between the medial and lateral malleoli in front of the ankle joint
At the base of the 5th metatarsal
questions.explanation: In front of the ankle joint, midway between the two malleoli, the anterior tibial artery becomes the dorsalis pedis artery (palpable just lateral to the extensor hallucis longus tendon).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: At which exact anatomical landmark does the femoral artery begin?
options: Midinguinal point (halfway between ASIS and pubic symphysis)
questions.explanation: The external iliac artery becomes the femoral artery behind the inguinal ligament at the midinguinal point (halfway between the ASIS and the symphysis pubis).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Cloquet’s (Rosenmüller’s) lymph node is the highest deep inguinal node located in the femoral canal and specifically receives direct lymph from:
options: The heel and lateral border of the foot
questions.explanation: Cloquet's node lies within the femoral ring and drains the glans penis/clitoris as well as deep inguinal afferents.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Denonvilliers’ fascia (rectovesical fascia) in males is located between:
questions.explanation: Denonvilliers’ fascia is the rectovesical septum separating the posterior prostate and seminal vesicles from the anterior rectal wall.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: During a low anterior resection, total mesorectal excision (TME) is performed within which anatomical plane to minimize local recurrence and nerve injury?
options: Avascular presacral space outside the mesorectal fascia (visceral fascia of rectum)
questions.explanation: Dissection in the 'holy plane' between the parietal pelvic fascia and visceral mesorectal fascia protects pelvic autonomic nerves and removes regional lymph nodes intact.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: During low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer, injury to the pelvic autonomic nerves running along the pelvic sidewall results in:
questions.explanation: Preservation of pelvic splanchnic nerves and hypogastric plexuses is critical to avoid postoperative urinary retention and sexual dysfunction.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Entrapment of the lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh beneath the inguinal ligament causes a painful dysesthesia known as:
questions.explanation: Compression of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve near the ASIS/inguinal ligament produces burning pain and numbness over the anterolateral thigh (meralgia paresthetica).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Explain the 'Ulnar Paradox': why is clawing of the ring and little fingers MORE severe in a distal ulnar nerve lesion at the wrist than in a high lesion at the elbow?
options: Because the radial nerve compensates in a high lesion

Because in a low wrist lesion, the medial half of flexor digitorum profundus (in the forearm) remains intact and actively pulls the DIP joints of the 4th and 5th fingers into unopposed flexion, whereas in a high elbow lesion FDP is paralyzed
Because the median nerve innervates the interossei in high lesions
Because the palmar cutaneous branch is spared at the elbow
questions.explanation: Intact FDP tendons in a distal ulnar nerve injury pull the IP joints into marked flexion while MCP joints hyperextend (unopposed extensors + paralyzed lumbricals/interossei), worsening the claw deformity.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: External hemorrhoids are covered by:
options: Modified skin (anoderm) containing somatic pain fibers
questions.explanation: External hemorrhoids are dilatations of the inferior rectal venous plexus located below the pectinate line, covered by somatically innervated anoderm.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Fracture of the medial epicondyle of the humerus directly endangers which nerve?
options: Ulnar nerve (lying in the groove behind the medial epicondyle)
questions.explanation: The ulnar nerve is subcutaneous behind the medial epicondyle ('funny bone') before entering the forearm between the two heads of flexor carpi ulnaris.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus or inferior dislocation of the glenohumeral joint most commonly injures which nerve?
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve winds closely around the surgical neck of the humerus; its injury paralyzes deltoid (flattening the shoulder contour and impairing abduction beyond 15°) and teres minor, with sensory loss over the 'regimental badge' area.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: From which artery do the princeps pollicis artery (to the thumb) and radialis indicis artery (to the lateral index finger) arise?
options: Radial artery (as it enters the palm between the 1st dorsal interosseous and adductor pollicis)
questions.explanation: Upon entering the palm, the radial artery gives off the princeps pollicis and radialis indicis arteries before continuing as the deep palmar arch.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: From which artery is the deep palmar arch primarily formed, and which branch completes it medially?
options: Primarily formed by the terminal part of the RADIAL artery (entering via the 1st dorsal interosseous space), completed medially by the deep palmar branch of the ulnar artery
Primarily formed by the ulnar artery
Formed by the posterior interosseous artery
questions.explanation: The deep palmar arch lies ~1 cm proximal to the superficial palmar arch directly across the bases of the metacarpals and interossei, supplied mainly by the radial artery.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: From which artery is the superficial palmar arch primarily formed, and which branch completes it laterally?
options: Primarily formed by the direct continuation of the ULNAR artery, completed laterally by the superficial palmar branch of the radial artery
Primarily formed by the radial artery, completed by the anterior interosseous artery
Formed equally by superior and inferior ulnar collateral arteries
Formed by the dorsal carpal arch
questions.explanation: The superficial palmar arch lies just deep to the palmar aponeurosis (at the level of the fully extended thumb's distal border) and is mainly derived from the ulnar artery.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: From which cervical fascia layer is the axillary sheath derived, and what structures does it enclose?
options: Investing layer; encloses axillary vein and long thoracic nerve
Prevertebral layer of deep cervical fascia; encloses the axillary artery and cords of the brachial plexus (plus axillary vein per Snell)
Pretracheal fascia; encloses subclavian vein only
questions.explanation: The axillary sheath is a tubular prolongation of the prevertebral fascia extending from the neck into the axilla around the axillary artery and brachial plexus cords.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: From which fascial layers of the abdomen is the femoral sheath derived?
options: External oblique aponeurosis anteriorly and internal oblique posteriorly
Fascia transversalis anteriorly and fascia iliaca posteriorly
Scarpa's fascia anteriorly and pectineal fascia posteriorly
Peritoneum anteriorly and obturator fascia posteriorly
questions.explanation: The femoral sheath is a downward prolongation of fascia transversalis anteriorly and fascia iliaca posteriorly for about 1 inch (2.5–4 cm) below the inguinal ligament.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: From which specific components of the brachial plexus does the long thoracic nerve (C5, C6, C7) arise?
options: Directly from the roots (C5, C6, C7)
questions.explanation: Both the dorsal scapular nerve (C5) and the long thoracic nerve (C5, C6, C7) arise directly from the roots of the brachial plexus in the neck.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Horseshoe abscesses in the perianal region spread by tracking around the rectum through which space?
questions.explanation: Infection originating in posterior crypts can track through the deep post-anal space into both ischiorectal fossae, forming a horseshoe abscess.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: How do efferent lymphatic vessels from the popliteal lymph nodes reach the deep inguinal lymph nodes?
options: Ascending through the adductor hiatus and adductor canal accompanying the femoral vessels
questions.explanation: Efferents from popliteal nodes travel upwards with the popliteal and femoral vessels through the adductor canal to reach the deep inguinal nodes.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: How does the anatomical relationship between the popliteal artery and popliteal vein change as they descend through the popliteal fossa?
options: The artery stays strictly medial throughout
The artery runs Medial → Deep → Lateral (M.D.L.) relative to the vein, while the vein runs Medial → Superficial → Lateral (M.S.L.)
The vein stays strictly posterior to the artery
They do not cross each other
questions.explanation: In the upper fossa, the vein is lateral to the artery; in the middle, superficial/posterior to it; and distally, medial to it (making the artery Medial, Deep, then Lateral relative to the vein).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: How does the anterior tibial artery enter the anterior compartment of the leg?
options: By passing through the adductor hiatus
By passing forward through an opening in the upper part of the interosseous membrane
By passing behind the lateral malleolus
questions.explanation: Arising at the lower border of popliteus, the anterior tibial artery passes anteriorly above the upper margin of the interosseous membrane into the anterior leg compartment.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: How does the axillary vein lie relative to the axillary artery throughout the axilla, and what separates them distally?
options: Lateral to the artery; separated by lateral cord
Medial to the artery; separated from it by the medial cord of the brachial plexus, ulnar nerve, and medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm
Posterior to the artery; separated by posterior cord
Anterior to the artery; separated by pectoralis minor
questions.explanation: The axillary vein lies medial to the axillary artery; between them run the medial cord, ulnar nerve, and medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: How does the median nerve cross the brachial artery in the middle of the arm?
options: Passes posterior to the artery from medial to lateral
Crosses anterior (superficial) to the brachial artery from lateral to medial
Remains strictly lateral to the artery throughout the arm
questions.explanation: In the upper arm, the median nerve lies lateral to the brachial artery; at the mid-arm (insertion of coracobrachialis), it crosses anteriorly from lateral to medial, lying medial to the artery in the cubital fossa.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: How does the tibial nerve change its relationship to the posterior tibial artery as it descends in the posterior compartment of the leg?
options: Runs Medial → Superficial (posterior) → Lateral (M.S.L.) relative to the artery
questions.explanation: The tibial nerve enters the leg medial to the posterior tibial artery, crosses posterior (superficial) to it, and lies lateral to the artery at the ankle.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: How does the ulnar nerve enter the hand at the wrist?
options: Deep to the flexor retinaculum inside the carpal tunnel
Superficial to the flexor retinaculum (lateral to the pisiform bone and medial to the ulnar artery) within Guyon's canal
Behind the styloid process of the radius
questions.explanation: The ulnar nerve and ulnar artery pass superficial to the flexor retinaculum in Guyon's canal, radial to the pisiform bone and ulnar to the hook of the hamate.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: How far distally does the saphenous nerve provide cutaneous innervation?
options: Down to the knee joint only
Down the medial leg, anterior to the medial malleolus, along the medial border of the foot up to the ball of the big toe (1st MTP joint)
To the tip of the 5th toe
To the sole of the heel
questions.explanation: The saphenous nerve is the longest cutaneous branch of the femoral nerve, extending along the medial foot as far as the head of the 1st metatarsal.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: How many lymph nodes typically constitute the popliteal group?
questions.explanation: Approximately 6 small popliteal lymph nodes lie embedded in the fatty tissue around the popliteal vessels.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: How many muscular branches does the ulnar nerve give off in the arm?
options: Zero (gives off no muscular branches in the arm, only an articular branch to the elbow joint)
questions.explanation: Neither the median nerve nor the ulnar nerve supplies any muscles in the arm (except the median nerve occasionally giving a twig to pronator teres just above the elbow).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Hyperabduction injury to the lower trunk of the brachial plexus (C8, T1—Klumpke's paralysis) causes:
options: Complete claw hand (paralysis of all intrinsic hand muscles—lumbricals and interossei) with sensory loss along the medial forearm and hand, plus possible Horner's syndrome (if T1 sympathetic fibers are torn)
questions.explanation: C8–T1 supplies all small muscles of the hand via the ulnar and median nerves; avulsion of T1 also disrupts preganglionic sympathetic fibers, causing ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis (Horner's syndrome).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: In a patient with chronic occlusion of the superficial femoral artery in the adductor canal, which vessels serve as the primary collateral pathway to bypass the block and perfuse the lower leg?
options: Profunda femoris artery (via perforating and descending lateral circumflex branches) anastomosing with the genicular branches of the popliteal artery
questions.explanation: The profunda femoris acts as the critical collateral lifeline of the thigh, connecting proximally via the cruciate anastomosis and distally via the genicular anastomosis.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: In an intersphincteric perianal abscess, pus accumulates between:
questions.explanation: Intersphincteric abscesses are located in the intersphincteric space between the internal and external anal sphincters.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: In cases of pelvic fracture with massive retroperitoneal bleeding, the primary source of arterial hemorrhage is typically branches of:
options: Internal iliac artery (e.g., internal pudendal, superior gluteal)
questions.explanation: The posterior and anterior divisions of the internal iliac artery supply the pelvic walls and viscera and are the primary source of life-threatening bleeding in unstable pelvic ring fractures.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: In females, the urethra is approximately how long?
questions.explanation: The female urethra is short (about 4 cm long), passing directly from bladder to vestibule anterior to the vagina.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: In males, the base of the urinary bladder is directly related posteriorly to:
options: Seminal vesicles and ampulla of ductus deferens
questions.explanation: The posterior surface (base) of the male bladder rests against the seminal vesicles and vas deferens.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: In pelvic fractures with disruption of the pubic symphysis, which part of the male urethra is most frequently torn?
questions.explanation: Shear forces at the prostatomembranous junction during pelvic ring fractures commonly cause posterior urethral disruption.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: In radical hysterectomy or low pelvic surgery, which ureteric relation is a frequent site of iatrogenic ligation?
options: As it crosses the pelvic brim
Where it is crossed anteriorly by the uterine artery ('water under the bridge')
Where it enters the bladder trigone
As it runs behind the renal vessels
questions.explanation: The ureter passes under the uterine artery near the lateral fornix of the vagina ('water under the bridge'), placing it at high risk during ligation of uterine vessels.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: In the female, what structure lies immediately anterior to the upper two-thirds of the rectum?
options: Sigmoid colon, ileum, and pouch of Douglas (rectouterine pouch)
questions.explanation: The upper two-thirds of the female rectum are separated anteriorly from coils of small bowel and sigmoid by the rectouterine pouch (Douglas’ pouch).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: In the male, what structure lies immediately anterior to the lower third of the rectum?
options: Base of the urinary bladder, seminal vesicles, and ampulla of vas deferens
questions.explanation: Anterior relations of the lower third of the rectum in males include the bladder base, seminal vesicles, and ampulla of the vas deferens.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: In the suprascapular notch, what is the anatomical relationship of the suprascapular artery and nerve to the superior transverse scapular ligament?
options: The suprascapular artery passes ABOVE the ligament, while the suprascapular nerve passes UNDER (through the notch beneath) the ligament
The nerve passes above and the artery passes under
questions.explanation: Classic anatomical rule ('Army over the bridge, Navy under the bridge'): the suprascapular artery runs above the transverse scapular ligament, whereas the suprascapular nerve passes through the foramen underneath it.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Injury to the common peroneal nerve at the neck of the fibula produces which characteristic clinical presentation?
options: Foot drop (loss of dorsiflexion and eversion, resulting in equinovarus posture and high-stepping gait) plus sensory loss over the anterolateral leg and dorsum of foot
Inability to flex the toes only
questions.explanation: Common peroneal nerve palsy paralyzes both the anterior (dorsiflexors) and lateral (evertors) compartments, causing unopposed plantarflexion and inversion (foot drop).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Injury to the deep branch of the radial nerve (posterior interosseous nerve) at the neck of the radius (e.g., Monteggia fracture) causes:
options: Wrist drop and complete sensory loss over the dorsum of the hand
Finger drop (loss of MCP extension of fingers and thumb extension) WITHOUT wrist drop (extensor carpi radialis longus is spared) and NO sensory loss
questions.explanation: Because extensor carpi radialis longus is innervated proximal to the bifurcation of the radial nerve, wrist extension (with radial deviation) is preserved, and the posterior interosseous nerve is purely motor.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Injury to the long thoracic nerve during radical mastectomy or axillary lymph node dissection causes paralysis of serratus anterior, resulting in:
options: Winging of the scapula (medial border protrudes posteriorly, especially when pushing against a wall) and inability to abduct the arm above 90 degrees
questions.explanation: Serratus anterior holds the medial border of the scapula against the thoracic wall and rotates the glenoid upward for overhead abduction (>90°).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Injury to the superior gluteal nerve results in paralysis of gluteus medius and minimus, leading clinically to:
options: Loss of hip extension when climbing stairs
Positive Trendelenburg sign (pelvis sags on the unsupported contralateral side)
Loss of sensation over the lateral thigh
questions.explanation: Gluteus medius and minimus abduct the hip and stabilize the pelvis during single-leg stance; paralysis causes a positive Trendelenburg sign.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Injury to the tibial nerve in the popliteal fossa or upper leg results in which foot deformity?
options: Calcaneovalgus (unopposed dorsiflexion and eversion due to paralysis of plantarflexors and invertors) with sensory loss on the sole
Loss of sensation in the 1st web space
questions.explanation: Tibial nerve paralysis eliminates plantarflexion (gastrocnemius/soleus) and inversion (tibialis posterior), leaving the foot pulled into dorsiflexion and eversion (calcaneovalgus).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Internal hemorrhoids originate from vascular cushions located:
options: Below the pectinate line in the perianal skin
In the submucosa above the pectinate line (typically at 3, 7, and 11 o'clock)
questions.explanation: Internal hemorrhoids are prolapsing submucosal vascular cushions located above the pectinate line at specific clock positions (3, 7, and 11 o'clock in lithotomy position).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Lymphatic drainage from the anal canal BELOW the pectinate line flows primarily into:
options: Medial group of superficial inguinal lymph nodes
questions.explanation: Because the lower anal canal is somatic/cutaneous, its lymph drains directly into the superficial inguinal lymph nodes.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Lymphatic drainage from the upper rectum goes primarily to which lymph node group?
options: Pararectal and inferior mesenteric lymph nodes
questions.explanation: Upper rectal lymphatics follow the superior rectal vessels to pararectal nodes and up to the inferior mesenteric lymph node chain.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Lymphatics from the urinary bladder drain into which lymph node groups?
options: External and internal iliac lymph nodes
questions.explanation: Lymphatic drainage from the bladder follows vesical vessels to internal and external iliac lymph nodes.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Mid-shaft fracture of the humerus (involving the spiral groove) typically injures which nerve and artery?
options: Axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery
Radial nerve and profunda brachii (deep brachial) artery
Ulnar nerve and superior ulnar collateral artery
questions.explanation: The radial nerve and profunda brachii artery lie directly against the bone in the spiral groove; mid-shaft humeral fracture causes wrist drop (loss of wrist/finger extension) and sensory loss over the dorsal 1st web space, while sparing triceps (whose branches arise higher).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Parasympathetic innervation responsible for micturition (contracting detrusor, relaxing sphincter) arises from:
questions.explanation: Parasympathetic fibers (nervi erigentes) originate from sacral segments S2-S4 to mediate bladder emptying.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Parasympathetic supply to the rectum and distal colon promotes:
options: Relaxation of internal sphincter and inhibition of motility
Contraction of internal sphincter and vasoconstriction
Peristalsis and relaxation of the internal anal sphincter
questions.explanation: Pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2-S4) provide parasympathetic motor supply to the distal gut and inhibitory input to the internal anal sphincter.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Pelvic fascia is condensed in certain regions to form important surgical ligaments, such as the cardinal (transverse cervical) ligament, which transmits:
options: Uterine vessels and autonomic plexuses to the uterus/cervix
questions.explanation: The cardinal ligaments extend from the lateral pelvic walls to the cervix/upper vagina, transmitting the uterine vessels.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Regarding the peritoneal covering of the rectum, which statement is completely accurate?
options: Upper 1/3 covered on front and sides; middle 1/3 on front only; lower 1/3 is uncovered
Entire rectum is covered by peritoneum
Only the lower third has a peritoneal coat
questions.explanation: Peritoneum covers the upper third on front and sides, middle third on the front only, and leaves the lower third completely bare.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Supracondylar fracture of the humerus in a child places which artery and nerve at immediate risk of laceration or entrapment?
options: Brachial artery and median nerve (particularly the anterior interosseous branch)
Profunda brachii artery and musculocutaneous nerve
questions.explanation: Posterior displacement of the distal humeral fragment in a supracondylar fracture can injure the brachial artery (risking Volkmann's ischemic contracture) and the median nerve.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Sympathetic innervation to the urinary bladder (inhibiting detrusor, contracting sphincter) arises from:
options: T11, T12, L1, L2 spinal segments
questions.explanation: Sympathetic preganglionic fibers originate from thoracolumbar segments T11-L2 via the superior and inferior hypogastric plexuses.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The arterial supply to the urinary bladder is derived primarily from branches of:
options: Internal iliac artery (superior and inferior vesical arteries)
questions.explanation: Superior and inferior vesical arteries branching from the anterior division of the internal iliac artery supply the bladder.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The ductus deferens crosses over which major vessel as it enters the pelvis from the inguinal canal?
questions.explanation: Entering the deep ring, the vas deferens hooks around the inferior epigastric artery and crosses external iliac vessels to enter the pelvis.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The external anal sphincter is composed of skeletal muscle and is divided into three parts:
questions.explanation: The external sphincter is voluntary skeletal muscle divided into subcutaneous, superficial, and deep portions.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The great (long) saphenous vein originates from the medial end of the dorsal venous arch and ascends:
questions.explanation: The great saphenous vein passes directly in front of the medial malleolus (accompanied by the saphenous nerve), making this the classic anatomical landmark for emergency venous cutdown.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The internal anal sphincter is a thickening of which muscle layer of the gut wall?
options: Skeletal muscle of the pelvic floor
questions.explanation: The internal sphincter is an involuntary smooth muscle thickening formed by the inner circular layer of the rectal muscle coat.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The ischiorectal (ischioanal) fossa is bounded medially by:
options: Levator ani muscle and external anal sphincter
questions.explanation: The wedge-shaped ischiorectal fossa is bounded medially by the levator ani and anal canal, and laterally by the obturator internus muscle.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The lateral members of the horizontal group of superficial inguinal lymph nodes drain lymph from:
options: The back below the level of the iliac crest
The upper half of the anal canal
The anterior abdominal wall above the umbilicus
questions.explanation: Lateral horizontal superficial inguinal nodes drain the gluteal region and back below the iliac crest.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The lateral plantar nerve supplies cutaneous sensation to which area of the sole of the foot (analogous to the ulnar nerve in the hand)?
options: Lateral 1½ digits (5th toe and lateral half of 4th toe) and most deep intrinsic muscles of the foot
questions.explanation: Analogous to the ulnar nerve in the hand, the lateral plantar nerve supplies the lateral 1½ digits and all interossei, adductor hallucis, lateral 3 lumbricals, and quadratus plantae.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The levator ani muscle consists of which three major subdivisions?
options: Superficial, middle, and deep external sphincters
questions.explanation: Levator ani is subdivided into puborectalis, pubococcygeus, and iliococcygeus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The medial members of the horizontal group of superficial inguinal lymph nodes receive lymph from all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Anterior abdominal wall below the umbilicus
Lower half of the anal canal
questions.explanation: The testis drains directly along the testicular vessels to the para-aortic (lumbar) lymph nodes, bypassing the inguinal nodes completely.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The medial plantar nerve supplies cutaneous sensation to which area of the sole of the foot (analogous to the median nerve in the hand)?
questions.explanation: Just like the median nerve in the hand, the medial plantar nerve supplies the medial 3½ toes and innervates abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis, flexor hallucis brevis, and the 1st lumbrical.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The median umbilical ligament is a fibrous remnant of which embryonic structure?
questions.explanation: The urachus (embryonic allantoic stalk) obliterates to form the median umbilical ligament extending from bladder apex to umbilicus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The middle rectal artery is typically a branch of which major vessel?
questions.explanation: The middle rectal artery arises directly from the anterior division of the internal iliac artery.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The most vulnerable site of iatrogenic injury to the male urethra during catheterization or instrumentation is:
options: Membranous urethra at the urogenital diaphragm
questions.explanation: The membranous urethra is fixed within the urogenital diaphragm and represents a narrow, less distensible segment prone to tearing.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The obturator internus muscle exits the lesser sciatic foramen after wrapping around which bony landmark?
questions.explanation: The tendon of obturator internus turns at a right angle around the ischial spine (lesser sciatic notch) to enter the lesser sciatic foramen.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The obturator nerve enters the medial thigh through the obturator canal accompanied by:
questions.explanation: The obturator nerve and vessels pass through the obturator canal in the superior pubic ramus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The patellar plexus of cutaneous nerves lying in front of the knee joint is formed by all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Intermediate and medial cutaneous nerves of thigh
questions.explanation: The patellar plexus is formed anteriorly by the infrapatellar branch of the saphenous nerve and the lateral, intermediate, and medial cutaneous nerves of the thigh.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The pectinate (dentate) line marks the junction between:
questions.explanation: The dentate line represents the embryological transition zone between endoderm (hindgut) and ectoderm (proctodeum), creating a major landmark for innervation, venous drainage, and lymphatic spread.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The rectosigmoid junction is clinically defined from inside by:
options: The termination of taeniae coli into a continuous outer longitudinal muscle coat
questions.explanation: At the rectosigmoid junction, the three separate taeniae coli spread out to form a continuous longitudinal muscle layer around the rectum.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The retropubic space (space of Retzius) is located between:
questions.explanation: The retropubic space of Retzius is an extraperitoneal fat-containing space between the pubic bones and the anterior bladder wall.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The seminal vesicles are located between:
questions.explanation: Seminal vesicles lie retrovesically between the posterior bladder base and the anterior rectal wall.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The transverse folds of the rectum (Houston’s valves) are permanent folds formed by mucous membrane and which muscular layer?
questions.explanation: Houston’s valves are formed by the mucous membrane folding along with the inner circular muscle layer (two on the left, one on the right).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The trigone of the urinary bladder is characterized by:
options: Presence of prominent mucosal folds (rugae) throughout
Being a smooth triangular area firmly adherent to underlying muscle, lacking rugae
Containing mucous glands and hair follicles
questions.explanation: The trigone is bounded by the two ureteric orifices and the internal urethral meatus; its mucosa is smooth and tightly bound because it lacks a submucosal layer.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The ureters enter the urinary bladder at:
options: The superolateral angles of the trigone
The anterior wall near the apex
questions.explanation: Ureters pierce the posterolateral wall of the bladder obliquely at the upper corners of the trigone, creating a valvelike antireflux mechanism.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The vertical group of superficial inguinal lymph nodes lies along the termination of the great saphenous vein and receives lymph primarily from:
options: The anteromedial superficial lymphatics of the lower limb
The posterolateral superficial lymphatics along the small saphenous vein
The deep structures of the foot
questions.explanation: Superficial lymphatics accompanying the great saphenous vein drain into the vertical group of superficial inguinal nodes.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Traction injury to the upper trunk of the brachial plexus (C5, C6—Erb-Duchenne palsy) produces the classic 'waiter's tip' deformity characterized by:
options: Adducted, medially rotated arm; extended, pronated forearm
Abducted, laterally rotated arm with flexed elbow
Hyperextension of MCP joints and flexion of IP joints
Wrist drop and loss of thumb opposition
questions.explanation: C5–C6 loss paralyzes abductors/lateral rotators (deltoid, supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor) and elbow flexors/supinators (biceps, brachialis, brachioradialis, supinator), leaving the limb adducted, internally rotated, extended, and pronated.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Venous blood from the superior rectal vein drains ultimately into which system?
options: Inferior vena cava via internal iliac veins
Portal venous system via inferior mesenteric and splenic veins
questions.explanation: Superior rectal vein drains into the inferior mesenteric vein, establishing the portal venous drainage of the upper rectum.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Venous drainage from the bladder forms a plexus around the neck and base that drains into:
questions.explanation: The vesical venous plexus drains into the internal iliac veins.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What are the anatomical boundaries of the quadrangular space in the posterior scapular/axillary region?
options: Superiorly: teres minor; Inferiorly: teres major; Medially: long head of triceps; Laterally: surgical neck of humerus
Superiorly: teres major; Inferiorly: latissimus dorsi; Medially: medial border of scapula; Laterally: humerus
Superiorly: supraspinatus; Inferiorly: infraspinatus; Medially: spine of scapula; Laterally: acromion
Superiorly: clavicle; Inferiorly: first rib; Medially: scalenus anterior; Laterally: coracoid process
questions.explanation: The quadrangular space is bounded above by teres minor (and subscapularis), below by teres major, medially by the long head of triceps, and laterally by the surgical neck of the humerus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What are the exact anatomical boundaries of the femoral ring (the upper abdominal opening of the femoral canal)?
options: Anteriorly: inguinal ligament; Posteriorly: pectineal ligament; Medially: lacunar ligament; Laterally: femoral vein
Anteriorly: fascia lata; Posteriorly: psoas major; Medially: femoral artery; Laterally: sartorius
Anteriorly: conjoint tendon; Posteriorly: pubic symphysis; Medially: femoral vein; Laterally: lacunar ligament
Anteriorly: sartorius; Posteriorly: adductor longus; Medially: gracilis; Laterally: pectineus
questions.explanation: The femoral ring is bounded anteriorly by the inguinal ligament, posteriorly by Astley Cooper's pectineal ligament, medially by Gimbernat's lacunar ligament, and laterally by the femoral vein.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What are the four terminal branches of the thoracoacromial artery (from the 2nd part of the axillary artery)?
options: Acromial, pectoral, clavicular, and deltoid branches
Suprascapular, dorsal scapular, subscapular, and circumflex scapular
Superior, middle, and inferior ulnar collateral and profunda brachii
Anterior, posterior, medial, and lateral thoracic branches
questions.explanation: The thoracoacromial trunk pierces the clavipectoral fascia and immediately divides into four branches: pectoral, acromial, clavicular, and deltoid (mnemonic: 'ABCD' / 'Cadavers Are Dead People').
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What clinical deformity results from a high median nerve lesion at the elbow when the patient attempts to make a fist?
options: 'Hand of benediction' (Pope's blessing)—index and middle fingers remain extended due to paralysis of FDS, lateral half of FDP, and lateral 2 lumbricals, while ring and little fingers flex normally
questions.explanation: In a high median nerve lesion, loss of FDS and the lateral half of FDP prevents flexion of the index and middle fingers during fist formation ('hand of benediction'), alongside ape-hand thumb deformity.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What does a positive Froment's sign (flexion of the thumb IP joint when trying to pinch a piece of paper) indicate?
options: Ulnar nerve palsy (weakness/paralysis of adductor pollicis, causing the patient to compensate using flexor pollicis longus innervated by the anterior interosseous/median nerve)
questions.explanation: Froment's sign tests adductor pollicis (deep branch of ulnar nerve); when weak, the patient substitutes thumb flexion via FPL (median nerve).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What forms the floor (anterior wall) of the popliteal fossa from above downwards?
options: Popliteal surface of femur, oblique popliteal ligament (knee capsule), and fascia covering popliteus muscle
Posterior surface of tibia and fibula only
questions.explanation: The deep floor of the popliteal fossa consists superiorly of the popliteal surface of the femur, centrally of the posterior knee capsule/oblique popliteal ligament, and inferiorly of the popliteus muscle.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What forms the superolateral and superomedial boundaries of the popliteal fossa?
options: Superolateral: biceps femoris; Superomedial: semitendinosus and semimembranosus
Superolateral: lateral head of gastrocnemius; Superomedial: medial head of gastrocnemius
questions.explanation: The diamond-shaped popliteal fossa is bounded superolaterally by biceps femoris, superomedially by semimembranosus/semitendinosus, and inferiorly by the two heads of gastrocnemius.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the anatomical course and termination of the small (short) saphenous vein?
options: Ascends anterior to medial malleolus and drains into femoral vein
Ascends posterior to lateral malleolus and drains into the popliteal vein
Ascends along the lateral thigh into the superior gluteal vein
Drains directly into the anterior tibial vein
questions.explanation: The small saphenous vein arises from the lateral dorsal venous arch, passes behind the lateral malleolus (with the sural nerve), and pierces the popliteal fascia to enter the popliteal vein.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the approximate length of the human rectum?
questions.explanation: The rectum measures approximately 5 inches (13 cm) in length, following the curve of the sacrum and coccyx.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the arrangement of the major neurovascular structures in the popliteal fossa from superficial (posterior) to deep (anterior)?
options: Popliteal artery → Popliteal vein → Tibial nerve
Tibial nerve → Popliteal vein → Popliteal artery
Popliteal vein → Tibial nerve → Popliteal artery
Common peroneal nerve → Popliteal artery → Popliteal vein
questions.explanation: From superficial (posterior) to deep (anterior) inside the popliteal fossa, the order is Tibial Nerve, Popliteal Vein, and Popliteal Artery (deepest, directly against the femur/capsule).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the arterial blood supply to the lower third of the rectum and anal canal?
options: Inferior rectal artery (branch of internal pudendal)
questions.explanation: The lower rectum and anal canal receive blood from the inferior rectal arteries branching from the internal pudendal arteries.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the cutaneous sensory distribution of the deep peroneal nerve?
options: Skin of the entire dorsum of the foot
Skin of the adjacent sides (web space) of the 1st and 2nd toes
Medial malleolus and medial border of the foot
questions.explanation: The deep peroneal nerve supplies all muscles of the anterior leg compartment and terminates cutaneously in the first dorsal web space (between the 1st and 2nd toes).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the cutaneous sensory territory of the median nerve on the palmar and dorsal aspects of the hand?
options: Palmar surface of the lateral 3½ digits (thumb, index, middle, lateral half of ring) and the nail beds (dorsal distal phalanges) of those same 3½ digits
Medial 1½ digits on both palmar and dorsal surfaces
questions.explanation: The median nerve supplies the palmar skin of the lateral 3½ fingers and wraps around to supply the dorsal skin over their distal phalanges.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the exact order of contents inside the cubital fossa from LATERAL to MEDIAL ('MBBR' / 'Really Need Beer To Be At My Nicest')?
options: Median nerve → Brachial artery → Biceps tendon → Radial nerve
Radial nerve (under brachioradialis) → Biceps brachii tendon → Brachial artery → Median nerve
Ulnar nerve → Brachial artery → Median nerve → Biceps tendon
Biceps tendon → Radial nerve → Median nerve → Brachial artery
questions.explanation: From lateral to medial within the cubital fossa: Radial nerve (deep to brachioradialis), Biceps tendon, Brachial artery, and Median nerve.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the exact order of structures passing behind the medial malleolus deep to the flexor retinaculum from anteromedial to posterolateral ('Tom, Dick And Very Nervous Harry')?
options: Tibialis posterior, Flexor digitorum longus, Posterior tibial artery & veins, Tibial nerve, Flexor hallucis longus
Tibialis anterior, Extensor hallucis longus, Anterior tibial artery, Deep peroneal nerve
Peroneus longus, Peroneus brevis, Sural nerve, Small saphenous vein
Flexor hallucis longus, Tibial nerve, Posterior tibial artery, Tibialis posterior
questions.explanation: From medial/anterior to lateral/posterior under the flexor retinaculum: Tibialis posterior tendon, Flexor digitorum longus tendon, Posterior tibial vessels, Tibial nerve, and Flexor hallucis longus tendon.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the functional composition of the anorectal ring palpable on digital rectal examination?
options: Puborectalis sling, deep external sphincter, and upper internal sphincter
questions.explanation: The anorectal ring is a crucial muscular ring formed by the puborectalis, deep external sphincter, and upper internal sphincter; its transection causes permanent fecal incontinence.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the landmark used during pudendal nerve block in obstetrics or perineal surgery?
questions.explanation: The pudendal nerve crosses the sacrospinous ligament near its attachment to the ischial spine, making the ischial spine the target landmark for infiltration.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the largest branch of the axillary artery, arising from its 3rd part?
options: Subscapular artery (which divides into circumflex scapular and thoracodorsal arteries)
questions.explanation: The subscapular artery is the largest branch of the axillary artery; it descends along the posterior axillary wall, gives off the circumflex scapular artery, and continues as the thoracodorsal artery to latissimus dorsi.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the largest branch of the posterior tibial artery, which runs in the posterior compartment near the fibula?
questions.explanation: The peroneal (fibular) artery arises from the posterior tibial artery ~2.5 cm below popliteus and descends along the fibula, giving a perforating branch to the ankle.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the main support of the uterus preventing prolapse?
options: Levator ani muscle (pelvic diaphragm) and cardinal-uterosacral ligament complex
questions.explanation: Apical support (cardinal/uterosacral complex) and level diaphragm support (levator ani) cooperate to maintain uterine position.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the maximum normal physiological capacity of the adult urinary bladder when fully distended?
questions.explanation: When fully distended, the adult bladder can hold 500 ml or more as it rises above the pubic crest into the hypogastric region.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the mechanism of the 'calf muscle pump' in venous return of the lower limb?
options: Contraction of gastrocnemius and soleus compresses the deep venae comitantes within the tight deep fascia (crural fascia), propelling blood upward while valves prevent reflux
Arterial pulsations push blood down the saphenous veins
Negative pressure in the popliteal fossa draws blood from the femoral vein
questions.explanation: During walking, contraction of the calf muscles within the unyielding deep fascia squeezes blood centrally through valved deep veins and draws blood inward through perforators.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the perineal body (central tendon of the perineum)?
options: A fibromuscular node anchored between the anal canal and urogenital diaphragm
questions.explanation: The perineal body is a vital fibromuscular junction where multiple perineal muscles converge, essential for pelvic floor integrity.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the primary action of the biceps brachii muscle when the elbow is flexed to 90 degrees?
options: Powerful supination of the forearm (in addition to elbow flexion)
questions.explanation: Biceps brachii is the most powerful supinator of the flexed forearm (e.g., driving a screw), whereas supinator acts best when the elbow is extended.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of the puborectalis muscle during continence?
options: To pull the anorectal junction anteriorly, maintaining the 90-degree anorectal angle
To compress the external urethral sphincter
questions.explanation: Puborectalis acts as a dynamic muscular sling that maintains the acute anorectal flexure, crucial for resting fecal continence.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the primary nerve supply to the levator ani muscle?
options: Direct branches from S4 (and pudendal nerve branches)
questions.explanation: Levator ani is innervated directly by anterior primary rami of S4 and the perineal branch of the pudendal nerve.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the primary sensory modality perceived within the rectum and upper anal canal?
questions.explanation: The rectum and upper anal canal possess autonomic innervation (inferior hypogastric plexus) and are sensitive exclusively to stretch, not somatic pain.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between the ulnar artery and the ulnar nerve in the lower two-thirds of the forearm?
options: The ulnar nerve lies strictly MEDIAL to the ulnar artery
The ulnar nerve lies strictly LATERAL to the ulnar artery
The ulnar nerve winds spirally around the artery
They are separated by the interosseous membrane
questions.explanation: In the middle and lower thirds of the forearm, the ulnar artery is accompanied on its medial side by the ulnar nerve, both lying beneath flexor carpi ulnaris.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the relationship of the cords of the brachial plexus to the SECOND part of the axillary artery (deep to pectoralis minor)?
options: All three cords lie lateral to the artery
They are named strictly according to their anatomical position around the 2nd part: Lateral cord is lateral, Medial cord is medial, and Posterior cord is posterior
All three cords lie anterior to the artery
Only the posterior cord is present
questions.explanation: The cords of the brachial plexus are named after their exact relationship to the 2nd part of the axillary artery behind pectoralis minor.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the standard length of the adult surgical anal canal?
questions.explanation: The anal canal extends downward and backward from the anorectal junction to the anus, measuring about 4 cm (1.5 inches).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the white line of Hilton (interscaphoid line)?
options: The junction between rectum and sigmoid
The intersphincteric groove felt internally between internal and subcutaneous external sphincters
questions.explanation: Hilton’s white line marks the intersphincteric groove position inside the anal canal, separating non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium from true perianal skin.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What lymphatic trunks drain the pelvic viscera into the systemic circulation?
options: Thoracic duct and right lymphatic duct
questions.explanation: Pelvic lymph eventually ascends via lumbar trunks into the cisterna chyli and thoracic duct.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What nerve innervates the external anal sphincter?
options: Inferior rectal nerve (branch of pudendal nerve, S2-S4)
questions.explanation: Voluntary control of the external anal sphincter is provided by the inferior rectal nerve (pudendal nerve, S2-S4).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What prevents urine reflux from the bladder back into the ureters during micturition?
options: Active sphincter muscles around ureteric orifices
Oblique intramural course of the ureter through the bladder wall muscle
High pressure in the renal pelvis
questions.explanation: The tunnel-like oblique course of the ureter through the detrusor muscle acts as a physiological one-way valve during bladder contraction.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What spinal segments contribute to the obturator nerve?
options: Dorsal divisions of L2, L3, L4
Ventral divisions of L2, L3, L4
questions.explanation: The obturator nerve arises from the anterior (ventral) divisions of L2, L3, and L4 of the lumbar plexus, whereas the femoral nerve arises from the dorsal divisions.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What structure marks the boundary between the greater (false) pelvis and lesser (true) pelvis?
options: Pelvic brim (pectineal line, arcuate line, sacral promontory)
questions.explanation: The pelvic brim (linea terminalis) forms the circular inlet dividing the abdominal false pelvis from the true pelvic cavity.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where are the infraclavicular (deltopectoral) lymph nodes located, and which territory do they drain?
options: Along the subscapular vessels; drain the back
In the deltopectoral groove below the clavicle along the cephalic vein; drain the lateral side of the hand, forearm, and arm
Deep to pectoralis minor; drain the medial breast
Along the axillary vein; drain the anterior abdominal wall
questions.explanation: Deltopectoral nodes accompany the cephalic vein from the radial side of the limb and send efferent vessels through the clavipectoral fascia directly to the apical axillary lymph nodes.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where are the roots and trunks of the brachial plexus anatomically located?
options: Inside the axilla behind pectoralis minor
In the posterior triangle of the neck (emerging between scalenus anterior and scalenus medius)
In the spiral groove of the humerus
questions.explanation: The roots (C5–T1 ventral rami) and trunks (upper, middle, lower) lie in the posterior triangle of the neck; the divisions pass behind the clavicle, and the cords lie in the axilla.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where are the supratrochlear (epitrochlear) lymph nodes located, and which region do they drain?
options: In the deltopectoral groove; drain the lateral hand and forearm
Just above the medial epicondyle (in front of trochlea); receive lymph from the medial side of the hand and forearm
In the cubital fossa; drain the shoulder joint
Posterior to the acromion; drain the scapular skin
questions.explanation: Supratrochlear nodes lie in superficial fascia above the medial epicondyle along the basilic vein and drain the medial (ulnar) hand and forearm before sending efferents to the lateral axillary nodes.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where do the deep inguinal lymph nodes lie, and through which opening do their efferents pass to the external iliac nodes?
options: Lateral to femoral artery; pass through adductor canal
Medial to femoral vein under fascia lata; pass through the femoral canal/ring
Inside the popliteal fossa; pass through obturator canal
Superficial to cribriform fascia; pass through saphenous hiatus
questions.explanation: Deep inguinal nodes (1–3 nodes) lie along the medial side of the femoral vein and drain upwards through the femoral canal into external iliac nodes.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where does lymph from the lateral quadrants of the breast primarily drain initially?
options: Anterior (pectoral) group of axillary lymph nodes
questions.explanation: Approximately 75% of breast lymph—especially from the lateral quadrants and nipple/areola—drains first into the anterior (pectoral) axillary nodes located along the lower border of pectoralis minor.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where does lymph from the lower medial quadrant of the breast have a potential pathway to spread, risking hepatic or pelvic metastasis?
options: Lymphatic plexus of the rectus sheath and subphrenic peritoneal plexus
questions.explanation: Lymphatics from the inferomedial breast communicate through the upper anterior abdominal wall with the subperitoneal/subphrenic plexus, allowing transcoelomic spread (e.g., Krukenberg tumor).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where does the adductor (Hunter's / subsartorial) canal begin and end?
options: Begins at the inguinal ligament and ends at the apex of the femoral triangle
Begins at the apex of the femoral triangle and ends at the adductor hiatus in adductor magnus
Begins at the greater sciatic foramen and ends at the knee joint
Begins at the saphenous opening and ends at the medial malleolus
questions.explanation: The adductor canal extends through the middle third of the medial thigh from the apex of the femoral triangle to the adductor hiatus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.
