questions.stem: Where does the axillary artery begin and where does it end?
options: Begins at the lateral border of the 1st rib (as continuation of subclavian artery) and ends at the lower border of teres major (becoming brachial artery)
Begins at the sternoclavicular joint and ends at the cubital fossa
Begins at the medial border of scalenus anterior and ends at pectoralis minor
Begins at the lower border of teres major and ends at the neck of the radius
questions.explanation: The axillary artery extends from the outer border of the 1st rib to the lower border of teres major, divided into three parts by the pectoralis minor muscle.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where does the basilic vein pierce the deep fascia of the arm to join the venae comitantes of the brachial artery and form the axillary vein?
options: At the middle of the medial side of the arm (basilic hiatus), continuing as the axillary vein at the lower border of teres major
At the lateral border of the first rib
questions.explanation: The basilic vein pierces the deep fascia near the mid-arm, accompanies the brachial artery, and unites with the venae comitantes at the lower border of teres major to form the axillary vein.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where does the great saphenous vein terminate?
options: Into the popliteal vein in the popliteal fossa
Into the femoral vein through the saphenous opening, ~4 cm below and lateral to the pubic tubercle
Directly into the external iliac vein above the inguinal ligament
questions.explanation: The great saphenous vein pierces the cribriform fascia at the saphenous hiatus (~4 cm inferolateral to the pubic tubercle) to join the femoral vein.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where does the nutrient artery of the humerus enter the bone?
options: Near the insertion of coracobrachialis on the medial aspect of the mid-shaft (directed downward toward the elbow)
questions.explanation: The nutrient artery arises from the brachial artery and enters the humerus near the coracobrachialis insertion, running distally toward the elbow ('to the elbow I go, from the knee I flee').
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where does the popliteal artery terminate by dividing into the anterior and posterior tibial arteries?
options: At the lower border of the popliteus muscle
At the neck of the fibula
questions.explanation: The popliteal artery ends at the lower border of the popliteus muscle by bifurcating into the anterior and posterior tibial arteries.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where does the posterior tibial artery terminate by dividing into the medial and lateral plantar arteries?
options: Deep to the flexor retinaculum (behind the medial malleolus)
In front of the ankle joint
At the lower border of popliteus
At the neck of the fibula
questions.explanation: The posterior tibial artery passes behind the medial malleolus deep to the flexor retinaculum and divides into medial and lateral plantar arteries.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where does the profunda femoris (deep artery of the thigh) arise from the femoral artery?
options: From the posterolateral aspect of the femoral artery ~4 cm (1.5 inches) below the inguinal ligament
questions.explanation: The profunda femoris arises from the posterolateral side of the femoral artery roughly 4 cm below the inguinal ligament and supplies the thigh compartments via circumflex and perforating branches.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where is the dorsal venous arch of the foot located?
options: Over the heads of the metatarsal bones
questions.explanation: The dorsal venous arch lies in the subcutaneous tissue over the heads of the metatarsals and gives rise to the great and small saphenous veins.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where is the neck of a femoral hernia sac located relative to the pubic tubercle?
options: Above and medial to the pubic tubercle
Below and lateral to the pubic tubercle
Above and lateral to the pubic tubercle
questions.explanation: Femoral hernias emerge through the saphenous opening below and lateral to the pubic tubercle, whereas inguinal hernias emerge above and medial to it.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where is the safe site for an intramuscular injection in the gluteal region to avoid sciatic nerve injury?
questions.explanation: The upper outer quadrant is safely away from the sciatic nerve and superior/inferior gluteal neurovascular bundles.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which anatomical structure lies immediately deep to the median cubital vein in the cubital fossa, protecting the underlying brachial artery during venipuncture?
questions.explanation: The bicipital aponeurosis separates the superficial median cubital vein from the deeper brachial artery and median nerve, preventing accidental intra-arterial injection.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which arteries form the arterial anastomosis BEHIND the medial epicondyle of the humerus?
options: Superior ulnar collateral artery + Posterior branch of inferior ulnar collateral artery + Posterior ulnar recurrent artery
Radial collateral artery + Radial recurrent artery
Anterior and posterior circumflex humeral arteries
Anterior interosseous and palmar carpal arteries
questions.explanation: Behind the medial epicondyle, the superior ulnar collateral and posterior branch of inferior ulnar collateral anastomose with the posterior ulnar recurrent artery.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which arteries form the arterial anastomosis IN FRONT OF and BEHIND the lateral epicondyle of the humerus?
options: In front: Radial collateral (anterior descending branch of profunda brachii) + Radial recurrent artery; Behind: Middle collateral (posterior descending branch of profunda brachii) + Interosseous recurrent artery
Superior and inferior ulnar collateral arteries
Princeps pollicis and radialis indicis arteries
questions.explanation: Around the lateral epicondyle, the two descending terminal branches of profunda brachii anastomose anteriorly with the radial recurrent artery and posteriorly with the interosseous recurrent artery.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which arteries form the arterial anastomosis IN FRONT OF the medial epicondyle of the humerus?
options: Anterior branch of inferior ulnar collateral artery (from brachial) + Anterior ulnar recurrent artery (from ulnar)
Superior ulnar collateral artery + Posterior ulnar recurrent artery
Radial collateral artery + Radial recurrent artery
Middle collateral artery + Interosseous recurrent artery
questions.explanation: Anterior to the medial epicondyle, the anterior branch of the inferior ulnar collateral artery anastomoses with the anterior ulnar recurrent artery.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which arteries form the cruciate anastomosis at the level of the lesser trochanter (providing collateral flow if the femoral artery is occluded)?
options: Inferior gluteal, transverse branches of medial & lateral circumflex femoral, and 1st perforating artery of profunda femoris
Superior gluteal and internal pudendal arteries
questions.explanation: The cruciate anastomosis connects the internal iliac system (inferior gluteal) with the profunda femoris system (medial/lateral circumflex femoral and 1st perforating arteries).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which arteries participate in the arterial anastomosis around the scapula (providing collateral circulation if the 3rd part of subclavian or 1st part of axillary artery is ligated)?
options: Suprascapular artery & deep branch of transverse cervical (dorsal scapular) artery (from subclavian) anastomosing with subscapular & circumflex scapular arteries (from 3rd part of axillary)
Anterior and posterior circumflex humeral arteries only
Superior and inferior ulnar collateral arteries
Internal thoracic and superior epigastric arteries
questions.explanation: The scapular anastomosis links the 1st part of the subclavian artery (via thyrocervical trunk: suprascapular & dorsal scapular) with the 3rd part of the axillary artery (via subscapular & circumflex scapular), bypassing occlusion between them.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which arteries participate in the genicular anastomosis around the knee joint?
options: Superior/inferior medial & lateral genicular branches of popliteal artery, descending genicular branch of femoral artery, descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral, and anterior tibial recurrent artery
questions.explanation: The rich genicular anastomosis around the patella and femoral/tibial condyles links the femoral, profunda femoris, popliteal, and anterior tibial arteries.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which arteries participate in the trochanteric anastomosis around the neck of the femur?
options: Superior gluteal, inferior gluteal, medial circumflex femoral, and lateral circumflex femoral arteries
Obturator and internal pudendal arteries only
questions.explanation: The trochanteric anastomosis is formed by the superior and inferior gluteal arteries anastomosing with ascending branches of the medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries; it provides the main blood supply to the femoral head.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which artery completes the deep plantar arch on the sole of the foot by joining the lateral plantar artery?
options: Deep plantar branch of the dorsalis pedis artery (entering via the 1st intermetatarsal space)
questions.explanation: The deep plantar branch of the dorsalis pedis dives between the two heads of the 1st dorsal interosseous muscle to anastomose with the lateral plantar artery, completing the deep plantar arch.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which artery provides the main blood supply to the upper third of the rectum?
options: Superior rectal artery (direct continuation of IMA)
questions.explanation: The superior rectal artery is the direct continuation of the inferior mesenteric artery supplying the upper rectum.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which artery provides the primary blood supply (~60%) to the lateral part of the female breast?
options: Lateral thoracic artery (branch of 2nd part of axillary artery)
questions.explanation: The lateral thoracic artery supplies approximately 60% of the breast (mainly lateral quadrants) via lateral mammary branches, while perforators of the internal thoracic artery supply the medial part.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which autonomic nerves provide sympathetic input to the rectum?
questions.explanation: Sympathetic fibers originate from T11-L2 via lumbar splanchnics and the hypogastric plexuses, mediating inhibition of peristalsis and contraction of sphincters.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which axillary lymph node group receives efferents from all other axillary lymph node groups and drains via the subclavian lymph trunk?
questions.explanation: The apical group lies at the apex of the axilla medial to the 1st part of the axillary vein; it receives lymph from the central, anterior, posterior, lateral, and infraclavicular nodes and forms the subclavian lymph trunk.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which branch arises from the FIRST part of the axillary artery (proximal to pectoralis minor)?
questions.explanation: The 1st part of the axillary artery gives off 1 branch (superior thoracic), the 2nd part gives 2 branches (thoracoacromial and lateral thoracic), and the 3rd part gives 3 branches (subscapular, anterior & posterior circumflex humeral).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which branches arise from the POSTERIOR cord of the brachial plexus (Mnemonic: 'ULTRA')?
options: Upper subscapular, Lower subscapular, Thoracodorsal, Radial, and Axillary nerves
Lateral pectoral, Musculocutaneous, and Lateral root of median nerve
Medial pectoral, Ulnar, Medial brachial cutaneous, and Medial antebrachial cutaneous
Suprascapular, Dorsal scapular, and Long thoracic nerves
questions.explanation: The posterior cord (formed by posterior divisions of all three trunks) gives rise to: Upper subscapular, Lower subscapular, Thoracodorsal, Radial, and Axillary nerves.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which cutaneous nerve supplies the skin immediately below the middle part of the inguinal ligament (over the femoral triangle)?
options: Femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve (L1, L2)
Lateral cutaneous branch of subcostal nerve (T12)
questions.explanation: The femoral branch of the genitofemoral nerve enters behind the middle of the inguinal ligament to supply skin over the femoral triangle.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which cutaneous nerve supplies the skin of the lower lateral quadrant of the buttock and the lateral aspect of the thigh down to the knee?
options: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh (L2, L3)
questions.explanation: The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (L2, L3) passes behind the lateral end of the inguinal ligament and supplies the lateral thigh and lower lateral buttock.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which cutaneous nerve supplies the skin of the posterior aspect of the thigh, popliteal fossa, and lower buttock?
options: Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve (S1, S2, S3)
questions.explanation: The posterior femoral cutaneous nerve arises from the sacral plexus (S1-S3) and runs down the back of the thigh beneath fascia lata.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which fascia separates the rectum posteriorly from the sacrum and presacral veins?
questions.explanation: Waldeyer's fascia (posterior mesorectal fascia) is the avascular plane behind the rectum that must be sharply dissected during rectal cancer surgery.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which intrinsic hand muscles are innervated by the recurrent branch of the median nerve and the digital branches of the median nerve (Mnemonic: 'LOAF')?
options: Lateral two lumbricals, Opponens pollicis, Abductor pollicis brevis, and Flexor pollicis brevis (superficial head)
All palmar and dorsal interossei and adductor pollicis
Medial two lumbricals and hypothenar muscles
Palmaris brevis and extensor pollicis brevis
questions.explanation: The median nerve supplies the 'LOAF' muscles in the hand; all other intrinsic hand muscles (hypothenar, interossei, adductor pollicis, medial 2 lumbricals) are supplied by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which ligament/fold connects the upper rectum to the sacrum posteriorly?
questions.explanation: The fascia of Waldeyer (mesorectal fascia) suspends the rectum from the sacrum and is a key surgical landmark in total mesorectal excision (TME).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which lymph nodes receive superficial lymphatics running alongside the small saphenous vein from the lateral foot and posterolateral leg?
questions.explanation: Superficial lymphatics along the small saphenous vein drain first into the popliteal lymph nodes embedded in the popliteal fossa fat.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which lymph nodes represent the primary sentinel station for lymphatic spread of cervical, vaginal, and distal rectal cancers?
options: Internal iliac and obturator lymph nodes
questions.explanation: Internal iliac and obturator lymph nodes receive primary drainage from deep pelvic viscera and genitalia.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which major structures are transmitted through Alcock’s canal?
options: Internal pudendal vessels and pudendal nerve
questions.explanation: The pudendal canal transmits the internal pudendal artery and vein, and the pudendal nerve.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscle exits the pelvis through the lesser sciatic foramen?
questions.explanation: The tendon of obturator internus turns sharply around the lesser sciatic notch/ischial spine to exit via the lesser sciatic foramen.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscle forms the main bulk of the pelvic diaphragm?
questions.explanation: The pelvic floor (diaphragm) is formed primarily by the paired levator ani and coccygeus muscles.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscle forms the medial boundary of the cubital fossa?
questions.explanation: The cubital fossa is bounded laterally by the medial border of brachioradialis, medially by the lateral border of pronator teres, and superiorly by an imaginary line between the humeral epicondyles.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscle forms the primary voluntary sphincter of the male urethra in the deep perineal pouch?
questions.explanation: The sphincter urethrae muscle surrounding the membranous urethra in the urogenital diaphragm provides voluntary urinary control.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscle in the anterior compartment of the arm is innervated by the musculocutaneous nerve AND assists in flexing and adducting the shoulder joint?
questions.explanation: Coracobrachialis is pierced and innervated by the musculocutaneous nerve and acts solely on the shoulder joint (flexion and weak adduction).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscle in the anterior thigh has a dual nerve supply from the femoral nerve and the obturator nerve?
questions.explanation: Pectineus is innervated primarily by the femoral nerve and frequently receives an accessory branch from the obturator nerve.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscle in the hand is responsible for abduction of the fingers ('DAB'—Dorsal Interossei Abduct) and is innervated by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve?
questions.explanation: Dorsal interossei abduct the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th digits away from the axial line of the middle finger; palmar interossei adduct them ('PAD'). All interossei are supplied by the deep ulnar nerve.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscle in the posterior thigh has a dual nerve supply from the tibial and common peroneal divisions of the sciatic nerve?
options: Biceps femoris (long head by tibial nerve; short head by common peroneal nerve)
questions.explanation: The long head of biceps femoris is supplied by the tibial division of the sciatic nerve, whereas the short head is supplied by the common peroneal division.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscle is the ONLY muscle in the forearm or hand innervated by the radial nerve proximal to its bifurcation into superficial and deep branches (aside from brachioradialis and anconeus)?
questions.explanation: Brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus arise from the lateral supracondylar ridge and are supplied by the main radial nerve trunk before it divides into superficial and deep (posterior interosseous) branches.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscle of the anterior arm is the primary pure flexor of the elbow joint regardless of whether the forearm is pronated or supinated?
questions.explanation: Brachialis inserts onto the tuberosity of the ulna (which cannot rotate), making it the pure workhorse flexor of the elbow in all forearm positions.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscle of the posterior compartment of the arm is innervated by the radial nerve in the spiral groove and helps stabilize the elbow joint?
questions.explanation: Anconeus is supplied by the branch of the radial nerve to the medial head of triceps within the spiral groove.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscle of the thigh has a dual nerve supply from both the obturator nerve and the tibial division of the sciatic nerve?
questions.explanation: The adductor portion of adductor magnus is innervated by the posterior division of the obturator nerve, while its hamstring portion (attaching to the adductor tubercle) is innervated by the tibial nerve.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscle of the upper limb girdle is innervated by the spinal accessory nerve (CN XI) rather than the brachial plexus?
questions.explanation: Every muscle acting on the upper limb is supplied by the brachial plexus EXCEPT the trapezius, which receives motor innervation from the spinal part of the accessory nerve (CN XI).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscles are innervated by the superficial peroneal (musculocutaneous) nerve?
options: Tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus
Tibialis posterior and flexor digitorum longus
questions.explanation: The superficial peroneal nerve innervates the lateral compartment muscles (peroneus longus and brevis—foot evertors) and supplies skin over the lower anterolateral leg and most of the dorsum of the foot.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscles are supplied by the lateral pectoral nerve vs. the medial pectoral nerve?
options: Lateral pectoral (from lateral cord) supplies pectoralis major; Medial pectoral (from medial cord) pierces and supplies pectoralis minor and the lower sternocostal part of pectoralis major
Lateral pectoral supplies subclavius; Medial pectoral supplies serratus anterior
Lateral pectoral supplies deltoid; Medial pectoral supplies latissimus dorsi
questions.explanation: The lateral pectoral nerve supplies pectoralis major, whereas the medial pectoral nerve pierces pectoralis minor (innervating it) to reach pectoralis major.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscles converge to form the perineal body?
options: Bulbospongiosus, superficial & deep transverse perinei, external anal sphincter, and levator ani
questions.explanation: The perineal body anchors the urogenital and anal triangles, receiving insertions from bulbospongiosus, transverse perinei, external sphincter, and levator ani.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscles form the floor (posterior wall) of the femoral triangle from lateral to medial?
options: Iliacus, psoas major, pectineus, and adductor longus
Vastus medialis, rectus femoris, and gracilis
Sartorius, tensor fasciae latae, and obturator externus
questions.explanation: From lateral to medial, the gutter-shaped floor of the femoral triangle is formed by iliacus, psoas major, pectineus, and adductor longus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which muscles in the anterior compartment of the forearm are NOT innervated by the median nerve (or its anterior interosseous branch)?
options: Flexor digitorum superficialis and pronator teres
Flexor carpi ulnaris and the medial half of flexor digitorum profundus (to ring and little fingers)—both supplied by the ulnar nerve
Flexor pollicis longus and pronator quadratus
Flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus
questions.explanation: Every muscle in the anterior forearm is supplied by the median nerve EXCEPT flexor carpi ulnaris and the medial half of flexor digitorum profundus, which are innervated by the ulnar nerve.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve accompanies the anterior tibial artery in the anterior compartment of the leg?
questions.explanation: The deep peroneal nerve descends along the anterior surface of the interosseous membrane alongside the anterior tibial artery.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve is exclusively motor and supplies the adductor muscles of the thigh (except the hamstring part of adductor magnus) plus gracilis and obturator externus?
questions.explanation: The obturator nerve innervates the medial (adductor) compartment of the thigh and sends a cutaneous branch to the medial thigh and an articular branch to the hip and knee.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve is most at risk of injury during harvesting or stripping of the great saphenous vein in the lower leg?
questions.explanation: The saphenous nerve accompanies the great saphenous vein along the medial leg and anterior to the medial malleolus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve pierces the coracobrachialis muscle and continues into the forearm as the lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm?
questions.explanation: Arising from the lateral cord, the musculocutaneous nerve pierces coracobrachialis, descends between biceps brachii and brachialis (supplying all three anterior arm muscles: 'BBC'), and terminates as the lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve provides somatic sensory innervation to the skin of the scrotum/labia majora and perineum?
questions.explanation: The pudendal nerve provides somatic sensation to the entire perineum, including scrotum/labia and the anal canal below the dentate line.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve runs directly on the anterior surface of the piriformis muscle within the pelvis?
questions.explanation: The sacral plexus lies on the piriformis muscle, with the large sciatic nerve emerging directly anterior to it.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve runs directly posterior to the 1st part of the axillary artery and lies on the superficial surface of serratus anterior?
options: Long thoracic nerve of Bell (C5, C6, C7)
questions.explanation: The long thoracic nerve (C5–C7) descends behind the 1st part of the axillary artery onto the external surface of serratus anterior.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve supplies both the obturator internus and superior gemellus muscles?
options: Nerve to obturator internus (L5, S1, S2)
questions.explanation: The nerve to obturator internus innervates obturator internus and the superior gemellus, whereas the nerve to quadratus femoris innervates quadratus femoris and inferior gemellus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve supplies latissimus dorsi and accompanies the subscapular/thoracodorsal vessels along the posterior axillary wall?
options: Thoracodorsal nerve (middle subscapular nerve, C6, C7, C8)
questions.explanation: The thoracodorsal nerve arises from the posterior cord and enters the deep surface of latissimus dorsi; it must be identified and preserved during axillary lymphadenectomy.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve supplies the gluteus maximus muscle?
questions.explanation: Gluteus maximus is solely innervated by the inferior gluteal nerve (L5, S1, S2).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve supplies the skin of the posterolateral lower leg and the lateral border of the foot up to the little toe?
questions.explanation: The sural nerve (formed by medial sural cutaneous branch of tibial nerve and sural communicating branch of common peroneal nerve) descends with the small saphenous vein to supply the lateral foot.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve supplies the skin of the upper medial aspect of the arm and floor of the axilla, and is NOT a branch of the brachial plexus?
options: Intercostobrachial nerve (lateral cutaneous branch of 2nd intercostal nerve, T2)
questions.explanation: The intercostobrachial nerve (T2) crosses the axilla to supply the skin of the upper medial arm; it is frequently encountered (and preserved if possible) during axillary lymph node clearance.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve supplies the skin over the medial side of the heel (heel pad)?
options: Medial calcaneal branches of the tibial nerve
questions.explanation: Medial calcaneal branches arise directly from the tibial nerve proximal to its bifurcation to supply the skin of the heel.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve supplies the skin over the shoulder cap (upper half of deltoid) and is derived from the cervical plexus rather than the brachial plexus?
options: Upper lateral cutaneous nerve of arm
questions.explanation: All skin of the upper limb is supplied by the brachial plexus EXCEPT the skin over the shoulder tip (supraclavicular nerves, C3–C4) and the upper medial arm (intercostobrachial nerve, T2).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve winds around the lateral aspect of the neck of the fibula, making it highly vulnerable to fracture or tight plaster casts?
questions.explanation: The common peroneal nerve leaves the popliteal fossa along the medial border of biceps femoris and wraps superficially around the neck of the fibula.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which neurovascular structures emerge ABOVE the piriformis muscle through the greater sciatic foramen?
questions.explanation: The superior gluteal nerve and vessels are the sole neurovascular structures passing through the greater sciatic foramen above the piriformis.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which neurovascular structures pass through the quadrangular space?
options: Radial nerve and profunda brachii artery
Axillary (circumflex) nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery and vein
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral vessels traverse the quadrangular space closely applied to the surgical neck of the humerus and inferior capsule of the shoulder joint.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics applies to the anal canal ABOVE the pectinate line?
options: Sensitive to somatic pain, touch, and temperature
Lined by stratified squamous keratinized epithelium
Lined by columnar epithelium and sensitive to stretch only
Drains into superficial inguinal lymph nodes
questions.explanation: Above the pectinate line, the anal canal is lined by columnar/transitional epithelium, supplied by visceral afferents (stretch-sensitive), and drains to internal iliac nodes.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics applies to the anal canal BELOW the pectinate line?
options: Sensitive to somatic pain via the inferior rectal nerve
Drained by the portal venous system
questions.explanation: Below the dentate line, the anoderm is somatic-innervated by the inferior rectal nerve (pudendal branch), making it exquisitely sensitive to pain, touch, and temperature.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a content of the adductor (Hunter's) canal?
questions.explanation: The femoral nerve divides in the femoral triangle; only its saphenous branch and nerve to vastus medialis enter the adductor canal alongside the femoral vessels.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which part of the male urethra is surrounded by the prostate gland?
questions.explanation: The prostatic urethra traverses the prostate gland from base to apex, receiving prostatic ducts and ejaculatory ducts at the verumontanum.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which part of the urinary bladder surface is covered by peritoneum in both sexes?
questions.explanation: The superior surface of the bladder is intraperitoneal, covered by peritoneum that reflects onto the anterior abdominal wall and uterus/rectum.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which pelvic muscle exits the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen?
questions.explanation: The piriformis muscle originates from the anterior sacrum and passes laterally through the greater sciatic foramen to the greater trochanter.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which peritoneal pouch is the lowest point of the peritoneal cavity in the erect or semi-recumbent female?
questions.explanation: The rectouterine pouch (Douglas' pouch) is the most dependent part of the female peritoneal cavity, where fluid or pelvic pathology accumulates.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structure divides the greater sciatic foramen into superior and inferior compartments?
questions.explanation: The piriformis muscle passes through the greater sciatic foramen, dividing it into suprapiriform and infrapiriform compartments.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structure forms the Lateral root and Medial root of the median nerve?
options: Lateral root from lateral cord (C5, C6, C7) and Medial root from medial cord (C8, T1)
Lateral root from posterior cord and Medial root from upper trunk
Both roots arise from the medial cord
Lateral root from C5 and Medial root from T1 only
questions.explanation: The median nerve (C5–T1) is formed anterior to the 3rd part of the axillary artery by the union of the lateral root (from lateral cord) and medial root (from medial cord).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structure forms the medial boundary of the femoral triangle?
questions.explanation: The femoral triangle is bounded superiorly by the inguinal ligament, laterally by the medial border of sartorius, and medially by the medial border of adductor longus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structure lies immediately LATERAL to the radial artery at the distal forearm (the classic site for palpating the radial pulse)?
options: Tendon of brachioradialis (and superficial branch of radial nerve in the middle third)
questions.explanation: At the wrist, the radial pulse is palpated directly against the distal radius between the tendon of brachioradialis laterally and the tendon of flexor carpi radialis medially.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structure passes through the upper triangular space (bounded by teres minor, teres major, and long head of triceps)?
questions.explanation: The circumflex scapular branch of the subscapular artery passes posteriorly through the upper triangular space to enter the infraspinous fossa and join the scapular anastomosis.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structures are enclosed within the femoral sheath?
options: Femoral nerve, femoral artery, and femoral vein
Femoral artery, femoral vein, and femoral canal (containing deep inguinal lymphatics)
Femoral artery and femoral nerve only
Great saphenous vein and femoral nerve
questions.explanation: The femoral sheath encloses the femoral artery (lateral compartment), femoral vein (intermediate compartment), and femoral canal (medial compartment). The femoral nerve lies outside the sheath.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structures exit the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen below piriformis, cross the ischial spine, and re-enter via the lesser sciatic foramen?
options: Sciatic nerve and posterior femoral cutaneous nerve
Pudendal nerve and nerve to obturator internus (with internal pudendal vessels)
Nerve to quadratus femoris and inferior gluteal vessels
questions.explanation: The pudendal nerve, internal pudendal vessels, and nerve to obturator internus exit below piriformis, hook around the ischial spine/sacrospinous ligament, and enter the perineum via the lesser sciatic foramen.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structures pass through the adductor hiatus into the popliteal fossa?
options: Femoral artery, femoral vein, posterior division of obturator nerve, and deep lymphatics
Great saphenous vein and saphenous nerve
questions.explanation: The femoral artery and vein pass through the adductor hiatus to become the popliteal vessels, accompanied by the genicular branch of the posterior obturator nerve and lymphatics.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structures pass through the anatomical snuffbox?
options: Radial artery (on the floor over scaphoid/trapezium), superficial branch of radial nerve (in roof), and cephalic vein (in roof)
Median nerve and flexor pollicis longus
questions.explanation: The radial artery crosses the floor of the anatomical snuffbox over the scaphoid to enter the 1st dorsal interosseous space, while the cephalic vein and superficial radial nerve cross its roof.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structures pass THROUGH the carpal tunnel deep to the flexor retinaculum at the wrist?
options: Median nerve, 4 tendons of flexor digitorum superficialis, 4 tendons of flexor digitorum profundus, and tendon of flexor pollicis longus (9 tendons + 1 nerve)
Ulnar nerve, ulnar artery, and median nerve
Radial artery, flexor carpi radialis, and median nerve
Palmaris longus tendon and superficial radial nerve
questions.explanation: Ten structures traverse the carpal tunnel: the median nerve plus 9 flexor tendons (4 FDS, 4 FDP, and 1 FPL). The ulnar nerve/artery pass superficially through Guyon's canal.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structures pass through the lower triangular space (triangular interval) below teres major, lateral to the long head of triceps, and medial to the humerus?
options: Axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery
Radial nerve and profunda brachii artery
Ulnar nerve and superior ulnar collateral artery
questions.explanation: The radial nerve and profunda brachii vessels exit the axilla inferiorly through the triangular interval to enter the spiral (radial) groove on the posterior humerus.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structures perforate the lateral intermuscular septum of the arm to enter the anterior compartment above the lateral epicondyle?
options: Radial nerve and anterior descending (radial collateral) branch of profunda brachii artery
Axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery
Median nerve and inferior ulnar collateral artery
questions.explanation: After traversing the spiral groove posteriorly, the radial nerve and radial collateral artery pierce the lateral intermuscular septum to lie between brachialis and brachioradialis anteriorly.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structures perforate the medial intermuscular septum in the middle of the arm?
options: Radial nerve and profunda brachii artery
Ulnar nerve, superior ulnar collateral artery, and posterior branch of inferior ulnar collateral artery
questions.explanation: The ulnar nerve descends medial to the brachial artery in the upper arm, then pierces the medial intermuscular septum (accompanied by the superior ulnar collateral vessels) to enter the posterior compartment and pass behind the medial epicondyle.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structures pierce the clavipectoral fascia (costocoracoid membrane) between the clavicle and pectoralis minor?
options: Cephalic vein, thoracoacromial artery, lateral pectoral nerve, and lymphatic vessels
Basilic vein, medial pectoral nerve, and ulnar nerve
Axillary artery, axillary vein, and radial nerve
Long thoracic nerve and thoracodorsal nerve
questions.explanation: Four structures pierce the clavipectoral fascia: cephalic vein, thoracoacromial artery (and vein), lateral pectoral nerve, and lymphatics passing to apical axillary nodes.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which superficial arteries accompany the superficial veins in the groin and arise from the femoral artery?
options: Superior gluteal, inferior gluteal, and internal pudendal arteries
Superficial circumflex iliac, superficial epigastric, and superficial external pudendal arteries
Medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries
Descending genicular and profunda femoris arteries
questions.explanation: The femoral artery gives off three superficial branches just below the inguinal ligament: superficial circumflex iliac, superficial epigastric, and superficial external pudendal.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which superficial vein ascends in the deltopectoral groove between the deltoid and pectoralis major muscles?
questions.explanation: The cephalic vein arises from the lateral end of the dorsal venous arch, ascends along the lateral arm, runs in the deltopectoral groove, and pierces the clavipectoral fascia to enter the axillary vein.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which tendons form the boundaries of the anatomical snuffbox on the posterolateral wrist?
options: Anteriorly (laterally): Abductor pollicis longus and Extensor pollicis brevis; Posteriorly (medially): Extensor pollicis longus
Flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus
questions.explanation: The anatomical snuffbox is bounded laterally by APL and EPB tendons, medially by the EPL tendon, with the scaphoid and trapezium forming its floor.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which test is performed before radial artery cannulation or harvesting (e.g., for coronary bypass) to confirm adequate collateral blood flow to the hand via the ulnar artery?
questions.explanation: The modified Allen's test occludes both radial and ulnar arteries while the patient clenches the fist, then releases the ulnar artery to verify rapid palmar flushing (<5–10 seconds) through the palmar arches.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which tributary of the great saphenous vein anastomoses with the lateral thoracic vein to form the thoracoepigastric vein (a caval-caval shunt)?
questions.explanation: The superficial epigastric vein communicates with the lateral thoracic vein, forming an important collateral pathway between the IVC and SVC.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which two nerves arise from the UPPER trunk (C5, C6) of the brachial plexus?
options: Long thoracic nerve and dorsal scapular nerve
Suprascapular nerve and nerve to subclavius
Lateral pectoral nerve and musculocutaneous nerve
questions.explanation: The upper trunk is the only trunk that gives off branches: the suprascapular nerve (to supraspinatus and infraspinatus) and the nerve to subclavius.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Why are femoral hernias particularly prone to strangulation?
options: Because the femoral nerve compresses the sac
Because the femoral ring is small and bounded by rigid, unyielding structures (especially the sharp medial edge of the lacunar ligament)
Because they always contain the urinary bladder
Because the femoral artery pulsates against the neck
questions.explanation: The tight, rigid margins of the femoral ring—particularly the sharp lacunar ligament medially—make femoral hernias highly susceptible to irreducibility and strangulation.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Why can hip joint pathology (such as osteoarthritis or Perthes disease) present clinically as referred pain to the medial side of the knee?
options: Shared innervation via the obturator nerve (which supplies both the hip joint and the knee joint/medial thigh)
questions.explanation: The obturator nerve supplies articular branches to both the hip and knee joints as well as cutaneous sensation to the medial thigh, explaining referred knee pain in hip disease.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Why do varicose veins develop when valves in the perforating veins become incompetent?
options: Blood flows from superficial to deep veins too rapidly
High-pressure blood from deep veins is pumped retrograde into superficial veins during calf muscle contraction
Arterial blood shunts directly into the dorsal venous arch
Lymphatic obstruction dilates the deep veins
questions.explanation: Normal perforator valves direct blood from superficial to deep veins; valvular incompetence allows high-pressure deep venous blood to reflux into the unsupported superficial veins.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Why does fusion of the membranous layer of superficial fascia (Scarpa's/Colles' fascia) to the fascia lata just below the inguinal ligament hold clinical importance?
options: It prevents extravasated urine in anterior urethral rupture from tracking down into the thigh
It anchors the great saphenous vein
questions.explanation: The attachment of Colles' fascia to the fascia lata along Holden's line prevents urine from descending into the thigh following bulbar urethral rupture.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Why does infection in the synovial sheath of the little finger (ulnar bursa) or thumb (radial bursa) carry a high risk of spreading to the opposite digit or forearm?
options: Because the radial and ulnar bursae frequently communicate with each other deep to the flexor retinaculum and extend proximally into the space of Parona in the distal forearm (horseshoe abscess)
Because they drain directly into the cephalic vein
Because they pierce the interosseous membrane
Because they connect with the shoulder joint capsule
questions.explanation: The flexor tendon sheaths of the thumb (radial bursa) and little finger (ulnar bursa) extend through the carpal tunnel into the forearm and often intercommunicate, allowing 'horseshoe' spread of tenosynovitis.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Why does the posterior tibial nerve remain vulnerable to entrapment in tarsal tunnel syndrome?
options: It passes through a fibro-osseous tunnel beneath the flexor retinaculum behind the medial malleolus
It runs subcutaneously over the lateral malleolus
It winds around the neck of the fibula
questions.explanation: Compression of the tibial nerve beneath the flexor retinaculum in the tarsal tunnel causes burning pain and paresthesia over the sole of the foot (tarsal tunnel syndrome).
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Why is an intracapsular fracture of the femoral neck associated with a high risk of avascular necrosis of the femoral head?
options: It tears the retinacular vessels derived from the medial circumflex femoral artery (trochanteric anastomosis)
questions.explanation: The femoral head depends predominantly on retinacular branches from the medial circumflex femoral artery traveling along the femoral neck capsule.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Why is cutaneous sensation over the central palm (thenar eminence/hollow of palm) SPARED in carpal tunnel syndrome?
options: Because the ulnar nerve supplies the central palm
Because the palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve arises proximal to the flexor retinaculum and passes superficial to it
Because the radial nerve supplies the palm
Because the palmar cutaneous branch enters Guyon's canal
questions.explanation: The palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve branches off in the distal forearm and runs above the flexor retinaculum, escaping compression inside the carpal tunnel.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Why must surgical ligation of the axillary artery NEVER be performed distal to the origin of the subscapular artery (3rd part) unless absolutely unavoidable?
options: Because the scapular collateral anastomosis bypasses proximal segments, whereas distal to the subscapular artery collateral flow to the arm is severely limited
Because it causes immediate necrosis of the clavicle
Because it severs the phrenic nerve
Because the brachial vein drains into it
questions.explanation: The rich scapular anastomosis connects proximal subclavian branches to the subscapular artery; occlusion distal to the subscapular artery compromises perfusion of the upper limb.
questions.source: Dr. Khalid Milad — supplied question bank
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which central nervous system structure serves as the primary integrative center containing the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) and the nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS) to mediate emesis?
questions.explanation: The vomiting center and CTZ are located in the medulla oblongata, coordinating emetic reflexes from peripheral and central inputs.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where do T-lymphocytes complete their final maturation, and what type of immunity do they mediate?
questions.explanation: T cells mature in the thymus, do not produce circulating antibodies, and mediate cell-mediated immunity requiring cell-to-cell contact.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: A 58‑year‑old man undergoes a left hemicolectomy for a transverse colon carcinoma. Intraoperatively the surgeon identifies a segment of the inferior mesenteric vein that drains the left colic artery and is found to be adherent to the posterior wall of the pancreas. Which of the following statements best describes the anatomical relationship that explains this finding?
options: The inferior mesenteric vein courses posterior to the pancreas and joins the splenic vein before forming the portal vein.
The left colic artery originates from the superior mesenteric artery and its accompanying vein lies anterior to the pancreas.
The inferior mesenteric vein is a tributary of the splenic vein and runs in the mesentery of the splenic flexure, which is in close proximity to the tail of the pancreas.
The left colic artery is a branch of the inferior mesenteric artery and its vein follows the posterior aspect of the pancreas as it enters the portal system.
questions.explanation: The inferior mesenteric vein (IMV) drains the left colic region and typically runs posterior to the pancreas, joining the splenic vein to form the portal vein. This posterior course explains why it can be adherent to the posterior pancreatic wall during a left hemicolectomy. The other options misstate the venous drainage or arterial origin, or incorrectly describe the vein’s relationship to the pancreas.
questions.source: Inferior mesenteric vein anatomy; portal venous system
questions.topic: Inferior mesenteric vein anatomy; portal venous system
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the therapeutic significance of HER2 overexpression in breast and gastric carcinomas?
options: It predicts resistance to all forms of surgical resection.
It predicts likelihood of response to HER2-targeted therapies such as trastuzumab.
It indicates benign biological behavior and eliminates the need for chemotherapy.
questions.explanation: HER2 status is a predictive molecular marker indicating responsiveness to targeted agents like trastuzumab.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which specific grading system is internationally established for evaluating breast carcinoma histology?
questions.explanation: Breast carcinoma is graded using the Nottingham system, which assesses tubule formation, nuclear pleomorphism, and mitotic count.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which clinical parameters are factored into the calculation of the Nottingham Prognostic Index (NPI) for breast cancer?
options: Patient age, serum albumin, and tumor location
Tumor size, grade of tumor, and lymph node stage
Presence of liver metastasis, smoking history, and CEA level
Body mass index and hormone receptor status alone
questions.explanation: The Nottingham Prognostic Index calculates breast cancer prognosis using tumor size, histological grade, and lymph node stage.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which medication has proven clinical value and FDA/scientific approval for the primary or secondary chemo-prophylaxis of breast cancer in high-risk individuals?
questions.explanation: Tamoxifen, raloxifene, and selective aromatase inhibitors (exemestane) are proven and utilized chemo-prophylactic drugs for reducing breast cancer risk.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the most common causative organism for a superficial skin or breast abscess?
questions.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is overwhelmingly the most common pathogen responsible for skin, soft tissue, and breast abscesses.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: A direct inguinal hernia typically protrudes through which anatomical landmark?
questions.explanation: Direct inguinal hernias push forward through the weakness of the inguinal (Hesselbach's) triangle, medial to the inferior epigastric vessels.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Above the arcuate line, how is the posterior wall of the rectus sheath formed?
options: By the aponeurosis of the external oblique alone
By the posterior lamella of the internal oblique and the aponeurosis of the transversus abdominis
questions.explanation: Between the costal margin and the arcuate line, the posterior rectus sheath is formed by the posterior lamella of the internal oblique and the transversus abdominis aponeurosis.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: An indirect inguinal hernia enters the inguinal canal through which opening?
questions.explanation: Indirect inguinal hernias enter the inguinal canal via the deep inguinal ring (congenital remnant of the processus vaginalis) and travel down the canal.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: At what vertebral level is the transpyloric plane located, marking the position of the pylorus of the stomach?
questions.explanation: The transpyloric plane is situated at the level of the L1 body, corresponding to the pylorus of the stomach, fundus of the gallbladder, and neck of the pancreas.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Behind which specific part of the pancreas is the portal vein formed by the union of the splenic and superior mesenteric veins?
questions.explanation: The portal vein is formed immediately behind the neck of the pancreas by the junction of the superior mesenteric and splenic veins.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: In the lower perineum, what is the direct continuation and specialized persistence of Scarpa's fascia called?
questions.explanation: In the perineum, the deep membranous layer of superficial fascia (Scarpa's fascia) persists as Colles' fascia, attaching on each side to the pubic arch.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Meckel's diverticulum is an embryological remnant of which structure?
questions.explanation: Meckel's diverticulum represents the unobliterated proximal part of the fetal vitellointestinal duct, typically located about 2 feet from the ileocaecal junction.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: The spleen is classically described by the mnemonic of numbers 1, 3, 5, 7, 9–11. What does "7" signify?
questions.explanation: The spleen dimensions and features follow: 1 inch thick, 3 inches wide, 5 inches long, 7 ounces in weight, and related to ribs 9–11.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What anatomical characteristic distinguishes the jejunum from the ileum?
options: Jejunal walls are thinner and narrower.
Jejunum features numerous prominent circular folds (plicae circulares) and fewer arterial arcades.
Jejunal mesentery contains abundant fat with no windows.
Ileum contains Peyer's patches on its mesenteric border.
questions.explanation: The jejunum has a thicker wall, larger/more numerous plicae circulares, simple arterial arcades (1-2), and less fat in its mesentery compared to the ileum.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What anatomical structure represents the obliterated fetal left umbilical vein?
questions.explanation: The ligamentum teres is the obliterated left umbilical vein, running within the free margin of the falciform ligament to the left branch of the portal vein.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What are Peyer's patches (aggregate lymphoid nodules) typically found on?
options: The antimesenteric border of the lower ileum
The lesser curvature of the stomach
The anterior surface of the liver
questions.explanation: Peyer's patches are large aggregations of lymphoid follicles located in the mucosa along the antimesenteric border of the lower ileum.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What are the exact boundaries of the lumbar (Petit's) triangle?
options: Anteriorly: external oblique; posteriorly: latissimus dorsi; inferiorly: iliac crest
Anteriorly: rectus abdominis; posteriorly: quadratus lumborum; inferiorly: inguinal ligament
Anteriorly: internal oblique; posteriorly: erector spinae; inferiorly: 12th rib
Superiorly: costal margin; medially: spine; laterally: mid-axillary line
questions.explanation: The lumbar triangle is bounded anteriorly by the posterior border of the external oblique, posteriorly by the lateral border of the latissimus dorsi, and inferiorly by the middle part of the iliac crest.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the classic rule of 2s often associated with Meckel's diverticulum?
options: 2% of people, 2 inches long, 2 feet from the ileocaecal junction
2 cm wide, 2 layers thick, 2 days of symptoms
questions.explanation: Meckel's diverticulum occurs in 2% of the population, is about 2 inches long, and lies 2 feet proximal to the ileocaecal junction on the antimesenteric border.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the direction of the fibers of the internal oblique muscle of the anterolateral abdominal wall?
questions.explanation: External oblique fibers run downward, forward, and medially; internal oblique fibers run upward, forward, and medially; transversus abdominis fibers run horizontally forward.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the normal physiological capacity of the adult gallbladder?
questions.explanation: The pear-shaped gallbladder has a capacity ranging between 30 and 50 ml.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What is the primary nerve supply of the Cremasteric muscle?
options: Genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve
questions.explanation: The cremasteric muscle is supplied by the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve, which causes it to elevate the testis.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What percentage of blood flow to the liver is delivered via the portal vein versus the hepatic artery?
questions.explanation: The liver receives roughly 70% of its blood volume from the portal vein and 30% from the hepatic artery (though oxygen delivery is split evenly at 50/50).
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What significant anatomical structure enters the rectus sheath precisely at the level of the arcuate line?
questions.explanation: The arcuate line marks the lowermost limit of the posterior rectus sheath wall, at which level the inferior epigastric vessels enter the rectus sheath.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: What type of hernia occurs when the sac protrudes through the linea semilunaris?
questions.explanation: A Spigelian hernia is defined as a hernia occurring through the linea semilunaris. Part 2: Stomach, Duodenum, & Small Intestine (Q16–Q28)
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where do the common bile duct and main pancreatic duct typically open?
questions.explanation: The ampulla of Vater opens into the second part of the duodenum on the posteromedial wall at the summit of the major duodenal papilla.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Where does the accessory pancreatic duct (of Santorini) typically open into the duodenum?
options: At the minor duodenal papilla (one inch above the major papilla)
questions.explanation: The accessory pancreatic duct opens into the second part of the duodenum at the minor duodenal papilla, roughly one inch proximal/above the major papilla.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which anatomical feature helps clinically identify the pylorus of the stomach during surgery?
options: Presence of rugae inside the mucosa
questions.explanation: The pylorus is identified by the thickening of the pyloric sphincter, an annular groove, and the prepyloric vein (vein of Mayo) running in front of it.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which area of the liver is completely devoid of peritoneal covering and directly contacts the diaphragm?
questions.explanation: The triangular bare area of the liver is bounded by the coronary ligaments and directly apposed to the diaphragm without peritoneal intervention.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which arterial branch supplying the lesser curvature of the stomach arises directly from the coeliac trunk?
questions.explanation: The left gastric artery is a direct branch of the coeliac trunk, whereas the right gastric artery typically branches from the hepatic artery.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which artery supplies the embryonic midgut derivatives (from the lower duodenum to proximal two-thirds of transverse colon)?
questions.explanation: The midgut is supplied by the superior mesenteric artery, originating from the abdominal aorta at the lower border of L1.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which cutaneous nerve segment supplies the skin immediately around the umbilicus?
questions.explanation: The level of the umbilical skin is segmentally supplied by the tenth thoracic nerve (T10), while the xiphoid is T7 and just above the inguinal ligament is L1.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which layer of the anterior abdominal wall gives rise directly to the internal spermatic fascia of the spermatic cord?
questions.explanation: As structures traverse the deep ring in the fascia transversalis, they acquire the internal spermatic fascia.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which ligament connects the hilum of the spleen to the left kidney and contains the splenic vessels and pancreatic tail?
questions.explanation: The splenorenal ligament connects the spleen to the left kidney, carrying the tail of the pancreas and splenic vessels.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which nerve provides parasympathetic innervation to the foregut and midgut?
questions.explanation: Parasympathetic supply to the foregut and midgut is delivered via the vagus nerve (anterior and posterior vagal trunks), whereas hindgut is supplied by pelvic splanchnic nerves. Part 3: Liver, Biliary System, Spleen, & Pancreas (Q29–Q40)
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which of the following contents passes through the superficial inguinal ring in the male?
questions.explanation: The superficial inguinal ring transmits the spermatic cord (in males) or round ligament (in females), along with the ilioinguinal nerve.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which part of the duodenum is completely invested by peritoneum (free and mobile) for its first inch?
questions.explanation: The duodenum is retroperitoneal except for the first inch of the first part, which has peritoneal attachments from the greater and lesser omentum.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which part of the pancreas lies directly within the concavity of the C-shaped loop of the duodenum?
questions.explanation: The disc-like head of the pancreas sits snugly within the C-shaped concavity of the duodenum.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structure forms part of the "stomach bed" (posterior relations separated by the lesser sac)?
options: Body of the pancreas and left kidney
questions.explanation: The stomach bed includes the transverse colon, transverse mesocolon, pancreas, spleen, splenic artery, left kidney, left suprarenal gland, and left crus of the diaphragm.
questions.approvalNote: Approved by the supervising physician per project instruction on 2026-11-15.

questions.stem: Which structure forms the conjoint tendon (falx inguinalis)?
options: Fusion of external oblique and internal oblique aponeuroses
Fusion of the lowermost fibers of the internal oblique and transversus abdominis
Lower rolled border of the external oblique aponeurosis
Fusion of rectus abdominis and pyramidalis
questions.explanation: The conjoint tendon is formed by the lowermost arching fibers of the internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles inserting into the pubic crest and pectineal line.
